title: Durin Web Console — choose the visual world
question: Glassmorphism is pinned. The roll assigned The Vitrine. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Vitrine
options.lineage: museum security display cases: laminated glass, etched labels, brass locks
options.thesis: Protected data sits behind layered security glass: visible to everyone, touchable only with a key Vault issued to a person.
materials: laminated glass panes with real blur depth
options.viewport: Overview as a gallery wall: one vitrine per tenant, protected values etched on the pane, and at each lock the signed-in person's brass key tag with its remaining minutes.
options.risk: Tips into museum theming if the cases decorate instead of marking the real authorisation boundary.

raised.raise: A single progress rail with a moving 'now' light runs every scenario (Protect → Break Glass), so the presenter always knows where the story is.
Every scenario step is a recoverable, deep-linkable state the presenter can jump back to.
Each tenant owns one tint of glass (ACME, Globex, Initech) used everywhere that tenant appears, never reused for anything else.
Time is drawn to scale: token TTLs and control-group windows are bars whose length is the exact seconds left.

options.label: Smart Privacy Glass
options.lineage: switchable PDLC office glass that turns clear when powered
options.thesis: Every protected value is frosted glass that clears only where Vault authorised you — the blur is the ciphertext.
options.viewport: A customer record as a wall of frosted panes; signing in as an operator clears them one by one while viewer stays frosted.
options.risk: The most literal reading of glassmorphism — familiar unless the clearing is always tied to a real Vault verdict.

options.label: Emission-Line Rail
options.lineage: glass spectrogram plates on a lightbox
options.thesis: One calibrated rail carries the whole console; state is line form — solid live, dashed pending, struck retired.
options.viewport: Scenarios as ticks on one rail; the open one blooms into a large glass plate above it.
options.case: Fuses well: key versions and TTLs read beautifully as line states; loses on audience identification — CISOs don't live in spectroscopy.
options.risk: Too austere for a live story; everything at one type size can flatten the verdict moments.

options.label: Cutaway Section
options.thesis: The stack drawn as a cutaway: browser, API, gateway, Vault and PostgreSQL with the walls removed and every part labelled.
options.viewport: One continuous section of the request path; each scenario lights the layer doing the work.
options.case: Strong product clarity for the Database Inspector; loses on audience identification and fights the pinned glass material.
options.risk: Reads as a children's-book explainer if the labels outnumber the evidence.

options.label: Step Sequencer
options.thesis: Scenarios as sixteen lit steps under a chase light.
options.viewport: One step row of the story with a running light.
options.case: Playful; wrong register for a security briefing.
options.kept: The chase light that always tells you where now is.

options.label: Fold Sequence
options.thesis: Thirty-two recoverable folds from square to crane.
options.viewport: Numbered fold steps in a margin column.
options.case: No audience link to data protection.
options.kept: Every step is a recoverable, deep-linkable state.

options.label: Gravity Rain Garden
options.thesis: Each cloud colour is its own force.
options.viewport: A garden whose rain obeys its cloud.
options.case: Beautiful, but surreal where the audience needs trust.
options.kept: One colour means one force, everywhere — here: one tint per tenant.

options.label: Dance Score
options.kept: Length encodes exact time — token TTLs drawn to scale.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean SaaS security dashboard: left nav, KPI cards, tables, one blue accent — glass as a light panel effect.
canonCard.viewport: KPI row, scenario cards, recent audit table.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every security vendor console.
